sections.content: How many people stayed in Wellingborough after gaining qualifications?

Wellingborough is a medium-sized town in the East Midlands. Wellingborough does not have its own university.

Wellingborough has higher levels of deprivation.

Overall, Wellingborough ended up with:

  • fewer graduates than it produced
  • fewer non-graduates with advanced qualifications than it produced
Note: all towns and cities in this analysis are defined based on population size only. This means that some cities are classed as towns because of their population.

Let's explore this further

There were 2,500 state-school pupils from Wellingborough who sat their GCSEs between the 2007 to 2008 and the 2010 to 2011 school years.

Of these, 675 (27%) went on to gain degree-level qualifications (level 6+ as defined by The Office of Qualifications and Examinations Regulation, or Ofqual ). We will call these people graduates.

Another 680 (27%) went on to gain other advanced post-16 qualifications, such as A-Levels, a foundation degree or higher apprenticeship (levels 3-5 as defined by Ofqual). In this tool, we will refer to these non-graduates with advanced qualifications as “qualified non-graduates", for brevity.

The charts below compare Wellingborough to other English towns and cities using three measures:

  • what proportion of Wellingborough's pupils became graduates or qualified non-graduates by the 2017 to 2018 academic year
  • of those graduates and qualified non-graduates, the percentages that lived in Wellingborough in the 2018 to 2019 academic year
  • how many graduates and qualified non-graduates from elsewhere came to live there by 2018 to 2019, relative to the number who sat their GCSEs there

In some towns, some of this information may not be available because of small sample sizes.
The size and deprivation level of a town, as well as the qualification levels of older residents, were all related to students' educational attainment. Read our previous analysis.

Where did those who left Wellingborough move to?

Of Wellingborough's graduates, 270 were living elsewhere in 2018/19.

However, 50 of those graduates (19%) were living fairly locally, in the Kettering and Wellingborough travel to work area (TTWA).

Of Wellingborough's qualified (level 3+) non-graduates, 220 were living elsewhere in 2018/19.

However, 95 of those qualified non-graduates (43%) were living fairly locally, in the Kettering and Wellingborough travel to work area (TTWA).

Of those in Wellingborough's GCSE cohort:

  • 170 graduates left the East Midlands
  • the most common region they moved to was London
  • 80 qualified (level 3+) non-graduates left the East Midlands

In 2018 to 2019, 24% of graduates and 26% of qualified non-graduates living in Wellingborough had moved there from elsewhere

In the 2018 to 2019 academic year, there were 510 graduates and 605 qualified (level 3+) non-graduates from our cohort living in Wellingborough. This is compared with the 675 graduates and 680 qualified non-graduates who had lived there when they sat their GCSEs.

In 2018 to 2019, 77% of the graduates had also lived in Wellingborough as GCSE pupils, while 24% had moved there from elsewhere.

Of the qualified non-graduates who lived in Wellingborough in 2018 to 2019, 74% had lived there as GCSE pupils, while 26% had moved to the area from elsewhere.
